lesley--lesleys-father: Lesley's father mends small machines, mostly clocks, in a shop on a street that runs down to the bay. The clocks hang on every wall, each one out of step, so the house ticks day and night. He lets Lesley stand on a crate at his bench and hold the parts. He tells a clock that will not start, "Don't sulk." For her last birthday he makes her a tin bird that hops and clicks its beak.

When the radio on his bench talks of Enders, he turns it down. On the wet night in 983 when an Ender comes, every lamp dies, but the clocks he wound by hand keep ticking. He tells the children to stay where they are. As the wall goes, he shouts Lesley's name from the doorway. Then the roof comes down. In the morning she finds him where the doorway had been.

Years later Chang'e gives Lesley a rifle with no cell and no cable: a spring, a pin and a bolt. Its bolt sounds like her father's bench with every clock going, and she thinks it will still work in the dark. On the morning the Storm Citadel's storm comes through the Singularity, violet light moves in the cloud over the bay again. Lesley remembers that only his hand-wound clocks kept ticking, and her thumb finds the old bolt.
lesley--ruby: When Ruby and Angela land at Selrick and ask for refuge, Lesley has already watched the record of the landing: Ruby's scythe raised over a child, then lowered. She lets the two in under watch. From that day her rifle is on Ruby.

In the Academy hall, Lesley stands before Ruby, Angela, Layla and Fanny with her hands behind her back. "Ruby, Angela: you are Aspirants as of today. The four of you stand together." Ruby keeps her eyes on the floor in front of Lesley's boots. Lesley tells them that by trusting each other they can gain limitless strength.

When the Singularity opens over the bay and Guinevere flies at it alone, Lesley sends the frontline after her on Layla's plan. Ruby runs through the hall with her scythe on her shoulder. "Your sector, Commander," she says on the channel, dry. Lesley's rifle has been on her since the day she landed. Ruby takes the order without a word against it.
lesley--vexana: Vexana's father, a Shield soldier, dies standing between her and an Ender, and she grows up in a home, training alone at dawn with a wooden pole. Years go by. One dawn Lesley stands at the yard's railings in a white officer's coat, a sheet with the home's stamp in her hand. "Father, Shield of Dawnbreak. Killed in action," she reads. Vexana waits for her to say she is sorry. She does not.

"I'm Lesley. The Academy tests its first intake this year. Come." Lesley folds the sheet and walks away without waiting for an answer. Vexana thinks that at the Academy she could break more Enders, and picks up the pole again.

Years later, when the Mother Matrix is knocked back, Vexana comes out of the black hole with Guinevere, in an Ender's robe. Lesley says she watched the Matrix fire on her, then watched her charge it. "You're on the line. Frontline assault, with Guinevere." Vexana grounds her staff and brings her heels together. "Understood, Commander." Chang'e says her file still says Missing. "Change it," says Lesley.
professor-joe--vexana: Professor Joe teaches the Combat Division, and Vexana sits his lesson on weak spots with Guinevere beside her. His last slide is a shaking recording from the Academy's oldest records: a ship of black blades over a city in a red sky. The Storm Citadel. Under its storm, every machine died.

On the day Ruby and Angela become Aspirants, Joe, still on his cane, sees the third years off at the gate portal. The dome is torn over the fish market. He sends the Layla-Fanny Team to the west end and Vexana and Guinevere to the east. Guinevere walks into the portal's light as if it had been lit for her, and Vexana follows without a word.

Dragged into the void, Vexana one day sees a violet storm turning far past the Mother Matrix, something huge and black-bladed inside it. She knows it from Joe's slide. On the night before the attack she climbs a ruined tower beyond the dome and sees the city's lamps still burning under the thunderheads. She remembers that every machine under that ship's storm died, and knows the ship itself is still behind the sky.
angela--fanny: Ruby and Angela come to Selrick off a black ship, and on the lot at the dome's foot the soldiers close in with rifles up. "Do you intend to take me back with you?" Angela asks softly. Fanny steps in front of the soldiers. "I watched them fight a giant for this city. Then they went with the soldiers so nobody else got hurt. I'll answer for them." On whose word? "Mine."
Chang'e sets the terms: Angela comes to the lab for an examination, and she and Ruby sit in the third-year class beside the two who vouched. Fanny says that is fair.

After the Mother Matrix is knocked back, Vexana comes back in an Ender's robe, and Lesley puts her on the line. Ruby tells Angela that Lesley did the same to them: watched first, then let them in. Fanny remembers the lot, the rifles and her word for Angela and Ruby. She watched Vexana fly at the Matrix's chest for this city, and she lets her blade points drop.
angela--layla: When Ruby and Angela land, Layla calls them armed newcomers. Fanny vouches for them, and Layla sighs. "Hers, apparently. And mine. Don't look at me like that. I only said they were funny in the head." Chang'e seats the two in the third-year class beside the pair who vouched. "Beside us?" says Layla.

Under the Singularity, Angela holds a bell of pink light around the four of them on a broken seawall. Enders press on it from every side, and each blow costs her a little. Layla stands on a slab in the middle with the cannon on her shoulder and calls the targets. Angela opens a pane in the shield, Layla's shot goes through, and Angela closes it before the next claw falls.

Soon the panes open before anyone asks. "Funny in the head," Layla mutters at Ruby and Angela, lining up again. "Both of you. The pane's open before I ask." "Thank you!" says Angela. Layla fires instead of answering.
change--researcher: The researcher works at the research base where Chang'e grows up. When he finds her at the big bench, standing on a box, he tells her it is for grown-ups and sends her back to her corner. After he sees the frame's first light, he looks from her to the cage. "The big bench is yours."

On the night the base falls, he carries Chang'e in from the yard and puts his own coat round her. In the nights after, he brings her soup and tells her of a home in the city, with beds and someone who cooks. She asks who would finish the frame. "It won't bring them back," he says. He never says "home" again, but he keeps bringing food.

He never leaves the base. Years later, when the Academy rises over the crater, Chang'e goes to him first for the Science Division's professors, and he becomes the first of them. Then she calls back the rest of her parents' old team.
change--ruby: "Good morning, Teacher Chang'e," says Ruby in her perfect voice, and brings Angela to the lab for her examination. Chang'e finds the empty socket where the Council's control unit was. Ruby pulled it out. Then Chang'e finds forty locked lines marked DANGER. Ruby says they are hers, a safeguard to stop Angela if Oro ever takes her again. Chang'e puts the lock on her list. "Then put me on the list too," says Ruby sweetly.

Ruby cuts the doll's live link to Oro in four seconds. Chang'e once spent a week cutting a link like that. When Ruby asks to read Mr. Bunny's code in turn, Chang'e refuses: he is her best friend. Then she hears what she has said, to the girl whose best friend she has just put on a list. She writes WEEKLY beside the lock anyway.

After Vexana goes missing, Chang'e cannot find the door Guinevere asks for. She sends her to Ruby, who comes each morning for Angela's check: "She does in four seconds what takes me a week." That morning Ruby deletes the lock, because Angela chooses it, and Chang'e draws a line through the last entry on her list. "Neat code. Shame to delete it." "Not really," says Ruby.
changes-father--lesley: Chang'e's father is one of the research base's two chief scientists, a quiet man who eats in silence. The Shield sends Lesley, its best young shot, to keep him, Chang'e's mother and the child they took in alive.

When Chang'e draws an eye for Lesley in secret, he sets its smallest parts with his tweezers. He asks whose eye it is once, and never again. When a fourth plate is set for Lesley at supper, he asks how much a soldier can carry and still run. "Thirty kilos," says Lesley. "Twenty, if she has to run far." He writes it on his napkin and keeps it.

He bends the steel tube of the frame for the first suit and weighs every plate under that napkin. When the Shield sends Lesley away on a top secret mission, the two Doctors walk her to the gate at dawn. He keeps his hands in his pockets. Then he takes one out, lays it on her shoulder, once, and puts it back.
changes-mother--lesley: Chang'e's mother is the other chief scientist of the research base, a warm woman who laughs with her whole face. When Lesley first comes to the gate and salutes, she smiles and holds out her hand anyway. Lesley only looks at it.

She sets a fourth plate at supper, and its chair faces the door. Later she puts a fourth stool by the frame, and at midnight Lesley's round stops there. Her notes for the frame begin with who it is for: "For whoever has to stand in front." Lesley reads the pinned page and stays for two more tests, though her round is waiting.

When the Shield sends Lesley on a top secret mission, the two Doctors walk her down to the gate at dawn. Chang'e's mother holds out her hand again. The first time, Lesley only looked at it. Now she takes it. "We'll set your plate," says Chang'e's mother.
fanny--girl-in-the-red-dress: At the breach of the dome, a little girl in a red dress stands crying on the pavement while people run around her. Professor Joe gives back her pink rabbit and covers her from a falling slab. Then a gold giant lowers its head through the broken dome, and the girl walks out into the avenue alone, her face turned up. The light in its chest grows.

Fanny sees her from the air. She drops and scoops the girl onto her left hip, the Shield's way, and the rabbit falls. "I'm flying!" says the girl. "Flying feels great," says Fanny, before the Shield part of her can stop it. The beam burns the place where the girl stood. Fanny leaves her behind a van, and her mother runs to her.

On the day of the Storm Citadel's attack, Fanny takes the bay road at roof height on her cable. The wind tears at her hair. Once she told a little girl on her hip that flying felt great. It still does. She grins, and for once the Shield part of her lets it be.
fanny--guinevere: On the morning of the Mother Matrix's attack, Fanny stands in the courtyard ranks beside Guinevere, under the billboard of Guinevere and Vexana back to back. The star at Guinevere's collar beeps, the pair's sound, which Fanny has not heard in weeks. "Guinevere?" says Fanny. On a roof stands a dark figure with a staff, Enders all around it. "That's her," Guinevere whispers.

The Shield soldiers swing their rifles up at the roof. Guinevere closes her mouth, and when the figure jumps she flies after it alone, without an order. Fanny has never once left her post without one. Still her first thought is that Guinevere must be in danger. She drops the Shield's way for Layla's map and tells Layla, "Lead."

In the Storm Citadel's attack the field kills Guinevere's drones and wings. In the bay road cut she breaks an Ender's core with her bare fist, and Vexana pulls her back through the gap in the wall. Fanny, holding the gap with plain steel, looks at Guinevere's side and her split knuckles. Then she moves to its edge and gives her the middle. "You saw it," Fanny calls along the wall. "Like that."
fanny--man-under-the-sign: On Fanny's first day at Selrick Academy, her VR assessment puts her in a broken street. A man shouts from under a fallen sign. "Simulated civilians are not scored," says a voice.

"Understood." Fanny pulls him clear first. It costs her eleven seconds. Then she fights the soldiers' way, her back to a narrow alley, and the Enders fall one or two at a time. Even with the eleven seconds, her time of 3:39 goes up above Layla's 3:41 on the rankings board.
fanny--professor-joe: Professor Joe wears a monocle and teaches the Combat Division. Fanny's first class with him puts her on his Team B3, with Layla and Roger. He teaches them that an Ender opens its chest only when it strikes. His last slide is a shaking recording from the Academy's oldest records: the Storm Citadel, a ship of black blades whose storm kills every machine under it.

At the breach he covers a crying girl and her pink rabbit from a falling slab, and it strikes him across the shoulders. Fanny is the one who then carries that girl out of the gold giant's path. Joe comes back on a cane, dissolves Team B3 and makes Layla and Fanny the Layla-Fanny Team, with one shared score: a kill is a point, a civilian carried clear is ten.

On the day of the Storm Citadel's attack, the ship comes down out of its black cloud over the Academy. Fanny has seen it once before, in a shaking film in Joe's class. Neither the film nor the sight of it coming through the mouth showed her how big it is close up. In the old record every machine under its storm died. She feels for her rig. It is still humming.
fanny--roger: Roger is the thin boy on Professor Joe's Team B3. He holds the pads while Fanny punches and tells her why Layla is like that: Fanny broke a record nobody had ever broken, on her first day, in front of everyone. "It's a board," says Fanny.

In their first VR drill together, Roger runs two hundred meters of open ground for the spot behind Layla and goes down on his back. An Ender rears over him. Fanny's cable wraps its claw before she has decided anything, and she hauls until it stops a meter above his face. Roger scores 2 kills. When Fanny and Layla argue after, he says, "Enough arguing, guys..." Nobody hears him.
When the siren calls Team B3 to a real breach, Roger does not get up. Fanny lifts him by the collar. "Protecting Terrinia is our duty."
fanny--ruby: Ruby and Angela land off a black ship, and on the lot at the dome's foot the soldiers raise their rifles. Fanny steps in front of the soldiers. She watched the two fight a giant for this city, she says. "I'll answer for them." A sergeant asks on whose word. "Mine." Ruby bows, names herself heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro, in another galaxy, and asks refuge of the school.
Chang'e lets them in on terms: the heir takes the entrance assessment, a droid follows the two everywhere, and they sit in the third-year class beside the two who vouched. "That's fair," says Fanny.

After the Mother Matrix is knocked back, Lesley puts Vexana on the line in her Ender's robe. Ruby leans to Angela: "She did that to us. Watched first. Then let us in." Fanny remembers rifles up at two girls off a black ship, and her own word for them. Now she has watched Vexana fly at the Matrix's chest for this city, and she lets her blade points drop.
fanny--tigreal: Fanny comes from a family of Shield soldiers, and Tigreal is her elder brother. On a ruined rooftop the night of the breach, she tells Layla about him: "An incredible fighter who I respect above anyone else." Since she was a kid she has longed to join him on the battlefield, but she could never quite reach his level. She hoped that if she gave every training her all, she would be good enough to fight beside him one day.
Layla understands then that Fanny was never looking down on her. She was looking past her, at him.

In the Storm Citadel's attack the field kills every suit, and Fanny holds the bay road cut with plain steel. Sitting against a tipped car, she says half to herself, "My brother would have held this street alone." Then she looks along the wall at the soldiers, and up at Layla. "I don't care what Tigreal would have done. I'm not doing it alone." She is not looking past Layla now.
guinevere--ruby: After Vexana is dragged into the dark, Chang'e sends Guinevere to Ruby. Guinevere waits in the lab doorway while Ruby deletes Angela's hidden code. Then she holds out her gold star. It beeps when Vexana is close, and she wants it to say where. Ruby runs green lines into the gold. "It has no direction, Guinevere. It only says yes."

At night Guinevere climbs to the observation lab in the Academy's tower, where Ruby and Angela keep the sensor array running, and searches the sky through the telescope. The first two nights they ask her to leave. On the third night nobody asks. She fills the night log beside Ruby's console with one word: Nothing.

Before dawn on the day of the attack, a faint point over the bay burns magenta and flashes. "Could it be Vexana?" Ruby reads the trace: likely an Ender, exceptionally powerful, trying to lure them in. "Guinevere. I said lure." "I heard you." "Then you know what it is." "I know what you read," says Guinevere. "I don't know what it is." Ruby saves the trace and keeps her gloved hand flat over it.
guinevere--selena: Selena sits in the front row of Guinevere's class, in late every morning with her guardian's note, her dragon-shaped machine clicking at her heel, asleep on her arms through lessons. When a boy on the Academy stairs called her dangerous, Selena waved her lollipop over her shoulder: "One day, when the haze clears..." Everybody laughed, Guinevere loudest. Guinevere has always liked her a little. She likes anyone who does not care what a room thinks of them.

In the Storm Citadel's attack, Obsidia's field puts out the Aspirants' lights one by one. Guinevere's gold light goes out last, far over the water, and from the bell tower Selena watches it drop. Since the charge, the open line has carried Guinevere's laugh. For weeks before that, Selena never heard it once.

Selena comes down into the bay road cut with the Enders behind her and stops over Guinevere and Vexana: horns, pointed ears, black claws, fangs. "Take a good look. This is the real me." Nobody laughs. Guinevere looks at her the way she looked at Vexana, past the plate and the claws, for the girl inside. For a breath Selena's smile goes. Then it is back, and she is gone.
layla--roger: Roger is Layla's teammate on Professor Joe's Team B3. Before a drill Layla smiles at him: "Scared, Roger? Hide behind me, then." "Okay," says Roger. He means it. With a minute left he runs two hundred meters of open ground for the spot behind her and goes down under an Ender. Fanny's cable stops its claw, and Layla's shot passes a finger from his face.

At the breach, Roger gets an arm under the hurt Joe and drags him toward a side street. Layla sees it and keeps walking. When Joe forms the Layla-Fanny Team, Roger goes to another pair. Joe says Roger reports that he falls down less.

In the bay road cut, a small boy stands crying behind Layla at the wall. Without turning she says over her shoulder, "If you're scared, you can hide behind me." Once she said it to Roger as a joke, and he ran across open ground for the spot behind her. She does not say it as a joke now. The boy takes a fistful of the back of her uniform and holds on.
layla--ruby: When Ruby and Angela land at the dome's foot, Layla calls them armed newcomers and says they are funny in the head. Still, when Fanny vouches for them, Layla sighs and adds her word: "Hers, apparently. And mine." Ruby bows and asks refuge of the school. Chang'e seats the newcomers beside the two who vouched. "Beside us?" says Layla.

Under the Singularity, the four of them stand on a broken seawall inside Angela's pink shield. Layla stands in the middle with her cannon and calls the strikes. "I've locked on to the enemies! Ruby, left. Fanny, high." Soon Ruby's scythe goes through the panes before anyone asks. "Funny in the head," Layla mutters at Ruby and Angela, lining up again. "Both of you. The pane's open before I ask."
lesley--lesleys-mother: Lesley's mother laughs from the kitchen door when her husband tells a clock not to sulk. "He says that to all of them." At the one table in the kitchen she decides who had the worst day, and that one gets the biggest piece. She keeps one candle stub in a drawer for birthdays. "Wish fast. And wish small. It's a small candle." Lesley wishes for a bigger candle, and her mother calls her sensible.

On the wet night in 983 when an Ender comes, she brings the lit candle upstairs, one hand cupped around the flame. "It isn't a birthday," says Lesley's brother. "No," says her mother. "It's for seeing." Then the wall goes and the candle goes out. As the roof falls she reaches past Lesley's father, one hand out toward the children's bed. In the morning Lesley finds her beside him and sits down in the rain between them.

Years later, on the night the research base falls, Lesley comes back minutes too late and finds Chang'e in the ash, her parents gone. Once Lesley sat in the rain between her own parents. She knows what this is better than anyone, and she has let it happen to Chang'e.
lesley--officer-who-posted-lesley: The officer has Lesley's file open on his desk. "Terrinia's research base," he says. "Two chief scientists, and a child they've taken in. You're the best young shot we have. Keep them alive." "Understood." Lesley takes it like any other mission.

When Lesley brings in a core piece whole, he comes out to the base himself. He will not give these orders over the comm. The piece makes her the most valuable shot the Shield has, he says, and she is going on a top secret mission, for as long as it takes, with no radio and no letters. Another soldier takes her gate.
Lesley sees that the piece has made her worth sending away, and sets it aside. In the Shield she has never refused an order. "Understood."
lesley--professor-joe: After Lesley and Chang'e make peace, Chang'e builds a glove wired to a dial that reads aspirant power. Lesley's hand goes in first, and the needle swings hard past the line. With the dial Lesley chooses her instructors. She tests only Shield soldiers she has fought beside, and most needles stop short of the line. One she keeps is a young soldier with a monocle, named Joe.

Over the crater the Academy rises wall by wall. On its first morning Lesley becomes its Chief Combat Instructor, head of the Combat Division, and Joe is one of its first instructors. Years later he is Professor Joe of the Combat Division, still with his monocle.
